text: You have to deliberately not act on the feedback of many of your early users, and this is at the same time as listening to people intensely and building what people want.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul about what people still don't understand about finding product market fit. Rahul explains one of the key counterintuitive insights from building Superhuman - that reaching product market fit requires deliberately ignoring feedback from certain user segments while intensely listening to others. He emphasizes that you can't build something that works for everyone, so the critical skill is knowing which feedback to act on and which to disregard.
text_ko: 초기 사용자(early users)들의 피드백(feedback)을 일부러 다 따르지 않아야 해요. 동시에 사람들 이야기를 깊이 듣고, 그들이 진짜로 원하는 것을 만들어야 해요.
text_zh: 你必须在一边深入倾听并打造用户真正想要的东西的同时，刻意不去按照很多早期用户的反馈去行动。
text_es: Tienes que decidir deliberadamente no actuar según la retroalimentación (feedback) de muchos de tus primeros usuarios, y al mismo tiempo escucharles con atención y construir lo que realmente quieren.
key_sentence: Deliberately not act on some feedback while listening to users intensely.
original_text: You have to deliberately not act on the feedback of many of your early users, and this is at the same time as listening to people intensely and building what people want. That's what we're here to do, is to make something that people want, but it can't be all people. And the question becomes, how do you listen to them? And then even of what they say, what do you pay attention to and what don't you?

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is intentional and purposeful, often implying careful consideration before taking action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, acting deliberately can refer to making strategic decisions based on thorough analysis rather than impulsive reactions, especially in response to feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: While it suggests a thoughtful approach, it can also imply a reluctance to act quickly, which may not always be appropriate in fast-paced environments.

vocabulary.definition: In a strong or extreme manner, often indicating a high level of focus or concentration.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, listening intensely to user feedback means engaging deeply with customer insights to inform product development and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of urgency and commitment, suggesting that the listener is fully invested in understanding the needs and desires of their audience.

text: This is a technique that I call the switch lock. It's born out of the observation that your calendar says what you thought you were going to do, but it's really only your trail of work that describes what you actually did.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul about his detailed time tracking system that helped him realize he was only spending 6-7% of his time on product, design, and marketing. Rahul describes his "Switch Log" technique, where instead of being constrained by calendar appointments, he tracks what he actually works on by messaging his assistant every time he changes tasks. This system revealed the gap between planned work and actual work, leading to organizational changes that improved his focus.
text_ko: 이건 제가 '스위치 락(switch lock)'이라고 부르는 기법이에요. 캘린더(calendar)는 여러분이 하려고 했던 일을 보여주지만, 실제로 무엇을 했는지는 오직 작업 흔적(trail of work)만이 말해준다는 관찰에서 나온 방법이에요.
text_zh: 我把这个技巧叫做“切换锁”（switch lock）。这个想法来源于一个观察：你的日历上写的是你打算做的事，但真正说明你到底做了什么的，是你实际留下的工作轨迹。
text_es: Es una técnica que llamo «bloqueo de cambio» (switch lock). Surge de observar que tu calendario refleja lo que pensabas hacer, pero en realidad solo el registro de tu trabajo muestra lo que hiciste de verdad.
key_sentence: Born out of the observation, your trail of work reveals actual accomplishments.
original_text: This is a technique that I call the switch lock. It's born out of the observation that your calendar says what you thought you were going to do, but it's really only your trail of work that describes what you actually did. How can we capture that? So I came up with the following idea. What if I just did whatever the heck I wanted?

vocabulary.definition: The act of carefully watching and noting phenomena or behaviors to gain insights or information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, observation is often used in market research to understand consumer behavior and preferences.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'observation' implies a passive gathering of information, it can also suggest a more analytical approach when used in a professional context.

vocabulary.definition: A method or way of doing something, often involving a specific skill or procedure.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup world, techniques can refer to innovative methods for product development, marketing strategies, or operational efficiencies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'technique' often implies a level of expertise or specialization, distinguishing it from more general methods.

vocabulary.definition: To give an account of something in words, detailing its characteristics or features.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, 'describes' is frequently used to articulate product features, service offerings, or project goals to stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'describes' is straightforward, it can carry a connotation of thoroughness or clarity, depending on the context in which it is used.

text: There is no such thing as a truly viral product. What I mean is, no app has sustained a viral factor of greater than one for any real period of time. Even Facebook in its heyday had a viral factor of about 0.7.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul about the secret to virality that he learned from Elliot Shmukler, LinkedIn's head of Growth. Rahul shares the counterintuitive insight that no product actually sustains true viral growth (where one user creates more than one new user) for extended periods. Instead, the real driver of sustainable growth is organic word of mouth - when users spontaneously recommend your product to others because they genuinely love it, not because of built-in viral mechanics.
text_ko: 진짜로 입소문 나는 제품(viral product)은 없어요. 제 말은 어떤 앱도 바이럴 계수(viral factor)가 1을 넘는 상태를 실제로 오랫동안 유지한 적이 없다는 거예요. 심지어 전성기 페이스북도 바이럴 계수가 대략 0.7 정도였어요.
text_zh: 其实没有真正能长期“走病毒”的产品。我的意思是，没有哪款App能在任何一段真实的时间里把病毒系数（viral factor）稳定维持在1以上。就连Facebook巅峰期的病毒系数（viral factor）也只有大约0.7。
text_es: No existe un producto verdaderamente viral. Me refiero a que ninguna aplicación (app) ha mantenido un factor viral (viral factor) por encima de uno durante un periodo sostenido. Incluso Facebook, en su mejor momento, tenía un factor viral de alrededor de 0,7.
key_sentence: No app has sustained a viral factor greater than one for long periods.
original_text: There is no such thing as a truly viral product. What I mean is, no app has sustained a viral factor of greater than one for any real period of time. Even Facebook in its heyday had a viral factor of about 0.7. It is word of mouth. It is the virality you can't measure that isn't a mechanic that isn't in a feature. It is when one user spontaneously tells another user about your product.

vocabulary.definition: Maintained at a certain level or rate over a period of time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'sustained' often refers to ongoing performance metrics, such as revenue growth or customer engagement, that remain consistent over time rather than showing temporary spikes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of stability and reliability, making it preferable in contexts where long-term success is emphasized.

vocabulary.definition: A metric that indicates the rate at which a product or service is shared or adopted by users, often measured as the number of new users generated by existing users.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech and startup world, understanding the viral factor is crucial for assessing the potential for organic growth and the effectiveness of marketing strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While a high viral factor is desirable, it can be misleading if not sustained over time, thus requiring careful analysis.

text: You can classify anything that you build in a company into one of two categories, solution deepening and market widening. Solution deepening means making your product better for its existing users, but not making it available to more users.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul what changed at Superhuman that made their product velocity feel faster. Rahul explains the difference between avoidable and unavoidable slowdowns. He introduces his framework for categorizing product development work: solution deepening (improving the product for current users) versus market widening (expanding to new user segments or platforms). Understanding this distinction helps explain why companies sometimes appear to slow down when they're actually doing necessary work to expand their market.
text_ko: 회사에서 만드는 모든 건 크게 두 가지로 분류할 수 있어요: 솔루션 고도화(solution deepening)와 시장 확장(market widening). 솔루션 고도화는 기존 사용자에게 제품을 더 좋게 만드는 것이지만, 더 많은 사용자에게 제공하게 하는 건 아니에요.
text_zh: 你在公司里做的任何东西，都可以分成两类：解决方案深化 (solution deepening) 和市场拓展 (market widening)。所谓解决方案深化，就是把产品做得对现有用户更好，但并不会让更多人用上。
text_es: Todo lo que desarrolles en una empresa se puede clasificar en una de dos categorías: profundizar la solución (solution deepening) o ampliar el mercado (market widening). Profundizar la solución significa mejorar tu producto para los usuarios que ya tienes, pero sin abrirlo a más usuarios.
key_sentence: Classify builds into solution deepening or market widening categories.
original_text: You can classify anything that you build in a company into one of two categories, solution deepening and market widening. Solution deepening means making your product better for its existing users, but not making it available to more users. Whereas market widening means making your product available to more users, but not making the product itself any better.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or organize items into categories based on shared characteristics or criteria.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, classifying products or services helps companies identify market segments and tailor their strategies accordingly.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'classify' is often used in formal contexts, it can imply a level of judgment about the categories being created.

vocabulary.definition: The process of enhancing a product or service to provide greater value to existing users without expanding its availability to new users.
vocabulary.businessContext: Solution deepening is crucial for retaining customers and increasing user satisfaction, often involving updates or new features based on user feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes a focus on quality and user experience rather than market expansion, which can be critical in competitive industries.

vocabulary.definition: The strategy of expanding a product's reach to new users or markets, often through marketing efforts or product adaptations.
vocabulary.businessContext: Market widening is a key growth strategy for companies looking to increase their customer base and revenue streams.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a proactive approach to growth, contrasting with solution deepening, which focuses on existing users.

text: The very presence of a reward halved their motivation. So what's happening? What's happening here, is researchers differentiate intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul about the difference between game design and gamification in product development. Rahul shares research from Stanford showing how external rewards can actually decrease motivation in children who were already interested in drawing. This study demonstrates why adding points, badges, and rewards (gamification) often fails - because external rewards undermine people's intrinsic motivation to engage with an activity they might naturally enjoy.
text_ko: 보상 자체가 있다는 것만으로도 동기가 반으로 줄었어요. 그럼 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는 걸까요? 여기서 연구자들이 말하는 건 내적 동기(intrinsic motivation)와 외적 동기(extrinsic motivation)를 구분하는 거예요.
text_zh: 一有奖励，他们的动力就减半了。那这是怎么回事？问题在于，研究人员把人的动机分成内在动机（intrinsic motivation）和外在动机（extrinsic motivation）。
text_es: La sola presencia de una recompensa redujo su motivación a la mitad. ¿Qué ocurre? Lo que pasa aquí es que los investigadores distinguen entre la motivación intrínseca (intrinsic motivation) y la motivación extrínseca (extrinsic motivation).
key_sentence: Rewards halved their motivation and massively undermine intrinsic motivation.
original_text: The very presence of a reward halved their motivation. So what's happening? What's happening here, is researchers differentiate intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation. With intrinsic motivation we do things because they are inherently interesting and satisfying, and with extrinsic motivation, we do things to earn rewards and to achieve external goals. That's the problem with rewards, is they just massively undermine intrinsic motivation.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or ascertain what makes something distinct or unique from others.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, differentiating products or services is crucial for competitive advantage and market positioning.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a careful analysis of features or qualities that set one entity apart from another, rather than just a superficial comparison.

vocabulary.definition: The drive to engage in an activity for its own sake, deriving satisfaction or fulfillment from the activity itself rather than external rewards.
vocabulary.businessContext: Intrinsic motivation is vital in fostering employee engagement and creativity, often leading to higher job satisfaction and productivity.
vocabulary.nuance: This concept emphasizes personal interest and internal satisfaction, making it more sustainable than motivation driven by external factors.

vocabulary.definition: The drive to perform an activity to earn external rewards or avoid negative consequences, such as money, praise, or recognition.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate environments, extrinsic motivation is frequently used to incentivize performance through bonuses, promotions, or other tangible rewards.
vocabulary.nuance: While effective in the short term, reliance on extrinsic motivation can sometimes undermine intrinsic motivation and long-term engagement.

text: For important decisions, you should be able to identify one, one reason that on its own supports the decision. It's based on the observation that all too often we rely on a collection of weak reasons to justify decisions.
speaker: Rahul Vohra
context: Lenny asks Rahul about his "Single Decisive Reason" (SDR) framework for decision-making. Rahul explains this technique he learned from Reid Hoffman at LinkedIn, where for any important decision, you must identify one reason that alone justifies the choice. This prevents people from using multiple weak arguments to support decisions and forces clearer thinking about what truly drives a choice.
text_ko: 중요한 결정을 내릴 땐 그 결정 자체만으로도 지지해 주는 '단 하나의' 이유를 딱 하나 꼽을 수 있어야 해요. 이건 사람들이 너무 자주 약한 이유들을 여러 개 늘어놓아 결정을 정당화하는 경우가 많다는 관찰에서 나온 얘기예요.
text_zh: 做重大决定的时候，至少得能说出一个——单凭它就能撑得住这个决定的理由。因为现实是，我们往往用一堆站不住脚的理由来为决定背书。
text_es: Para decisiones importantes, deberías poder identificar una sola razón que, por sí sola, respalde la decisión. Esto se basa en la observación de que, con demasiada frecuencia, nos apoyamos en un conjunto de razones endebles para justificarlas.
key_sentence: Identify one reason that on its own supports important decisions.
original_text: For important decisions, you should be able to identify one, one reason that on its own supports the decision. It's based on the observation that all too often we rely on a collection of weak reasons to justify decisions. If they can't yet isolate it, that tells me they haven't yet figured out why they want to make the decision.

vocabulary.definition: To recognize or establish the identity of something or someone, often through analysis or examination.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, identifying key issues, opportunities, or stakeholders is crucial for strategic planning and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'identify' implies a clear recognition, it can also suggest a deeper analysis rather than a superficial acknowledgment.

vocabulary.definition: To provide valid reasons or explanations for a decision, action, or belief, demonstrating its appropriateness or necessity.
vocabulary.businessContext: Justifying decisions in a business context often involves presenting data or logical arguments to stakeholders to gain their support or approval.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of defending a position, which may imply that the justification is necessary due to potential scrutiny.

vocabulary.definition: The act of carefully watching or monitoring something to gather information or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, observation is critical for market research, performance evaluation, and understanding customer behavior, leading to informed decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'observation' implies a passive act of watching, it can also suggest active engagement and analysis, depending on the context.
